proposals.title: Directed Graph for Corridor Requirement Dependency Chains
proposals.problem_solved: Requirements reference each other. A flat list cannot represent these dependencies, making timeline ordering manual and error-prone.
proposals.description: Model corridor steps as a DAG: each step lists prerequisite_step_ids. At YAML load, _reject_prerequisite_cycles refuses a circular graph. At schedule time, Kahn's algorithm in _topological_order emits a legal order and raises on a cycle.

implementation_notes.data_shape: CorridorStep.prerequisite_step_ids in pathway YAML; persisted as rce.steps.prerequisite_step_ids uuid[]
implementation_notes.lawyer_gate: Pathway YAML cites rules; serving still only emits review_status='approved' requirement_items. Do not invent a separate edge table for lawyer sign-off.

proposals.relopass_payoff: Circular authoring fails at load, not a live case. Delay on an upstream step shifts every downstream date.

grounding.actual_component: Corridor Agent YAML step graph + rce persistence
grounding.do_not: Do not add WorkspaceDB tables requirement_nodes / requirement_edges. The graph already lives in git YAML and rce.steps.

proposals.title: Trie for Corridor-Code Lookup and Prefix Discovery
proposals.component: Case Command — corridor selector / expansion map
proposals.problem_solved: Finding all corridors originating in FR or autocompleting FR-N becomes a slow full-table scan as the map grows toward ~120 pairs.
proposals.description: Index corridor codes in a trie keyed on origin/destination prefix. Lookup is O(length of corridor code) regardless of total corridor count.

implementation_notes.key_structure: Canonical key is ORIGIN_DEST (underscore), loaded into an in-memory dict at first read
key_operations: list_corridors linear scan of 13 YAML profiles
implementation_notes.memory_note: 13 corridor.yaml files. A trie would add code without a measured win.

proposals.relopass_payoff: Prefix discovery over 13 YAML profiles is a linear scan of a handful of strings. A trie would add code without a measured win.
proposals.effort_estimate: None — revisit only if ~120 served corridors exist

grounding.do_not: Do not build a trie at current scale. There is no WorkspaceDB corridor table to index.

proposals.title: Hash-Map Serving Index for Requirement Facts
proposals.cs_concept: Hash table — O(1) average lookup via hash function + chaining
proposals.problem_solved: Serving a case is read-heavy and latency-sensitive. Fetching requirement facts currently requires a DB scan or multi-join query on each case load.
proposals.description: The original proposal loaded requirement_facts into a Node.js Map or Redis hash keyed {corridor}:{employee_type}:{fact_key}. That table and runtime are not the serving path. Dossier serving is a keyed Postgres filter on public.requirement_items.

implementation_notes.key_format: Serving key is (country_code, purpose, review_status='approved') on public.requirement_items
implementation_notes.collision_note: Composite SQL key, not a hash-map collision domain. Do not conflate with immigration_requirements (corridor × visa_type).

proposals.relopass_payoff: Indexed lookup already exists. A process-local cache is a time–space trade-off only after a measured p95 on list_requirements — not a speculative Redis/Node map.

grounding.actual_component: public.requirement_items via crud.list_requirements (dossier) and immigration_requirements (entry-visa checklist)
grounding.do_not: Do not invent a serving cache in Node or Redis. Do not key the dossier on {corridor}:{employee_type}:{fact_key} — that conflates the destination-only dossier with the corridor×visa immigration engine. requirement_facts is not the served catalog.

proposals.title: Binary Decision Tree for Compliance Branching Logic
proposals.cs_concept: Binary search tree — ordered left/right branching
proposals.problem_solved: EU citizen → path A vs. non-EU passport → path B is nested if/else in code, making lawyer review impossible without reading source files.
proposals.description: Pathway YAML already stores eligibility_logic.branches (cited, requires_all, verdict_on_pass). That is a data-driven decision graph, not a BST. Family/STA filters still live in Python rules_engine. evaluate(corridor, case) is still out of scope in corridor_persistence.

key_operations: load-time structural validation of branch cites
planned evaluate() walk — not yet wired
implementation_notes.where: corridors/<ID>/pathways/*/v1.yaml + backend/relopass/corridors/loader.py; remaining code branches in backend/app/services/rules_engine.py
implementation_notes.trust_architecture: Cited YAML branches are the lawyer-reviewable claims. Do not externalise them into a BST of left/right child rows.

proposals.relopass_payoff: Lawyer-reviewable branching already exists as YAML claims with citations. The remaining work is wiring evaluate() and showing the taken branch in HR UI — not a decision_nodes table and not a BST (eligibility is not ordered-search).

grounding.do_not: Do not store a BST in WorkspaceDB. Do not rewrite rules_engine into left/right child rows. Eligibility is a cited predicate graph, not binary search. Do not wire evaluate() in this backlog pass.

proposals.title: Linked-List Timeline for Ordered Requirement Steps
proposals.cs_concept: Linked list — O(1) insertion, preserved sequence, no renumbering
proposals.problem_solved: A newly discovered step cannot be cheaply inserted into a fixed-index array without renumbering every subsequent step.
proposals.description: Store timeline steps as a linked/sequenced structure with next_step_id. Inserting a new step is a pointer swap.

implementation_notes.data_shape: Already: prerequisite_step_ids[] on each step — a DAG, not a singly-linked list
key_operations: insert an edge by editing two YAML lists
implementation_notes.ux_note: Authoring insert is add a YAML node plus prerequisite edges, not a next_step_id pointer swap.

proposals.relopass_payoff: A linked list cannot represent diamond dependencies. The DAG already supports inserting a step without renumbering — add the node and two prerequisite edges.
proposals.effort_estimate: None — linked list would be a regression

grounding.actual_component: DAG via prerequisite_step_ids (IE→ES diamond is the worked example)
grounding.do_not: Do not add next_step_id overlay tables. A linked list cannot encode a step with two parents.

proposals.title: Access-Pattern-Driven Data Architecture Audit
proposals.cs_concept: Time–space trade-off — dominant operation dictates the structure
proposals.problem_solved: Forcing one shape onto mismatched operations creates slow queries and brittle authoring.
proposals.description: Audit each access pattern against the structure that actually exists. Document the mapping as an ADR. Do not invent WorkspaceDB tables to match the lecture. ADR-003 already records this mapping; cite it, do not rewrite it as a second source of truth.

audit_targets: corridor registry — in-memory dict, prefix = linear scan of 13 profiles
timeline steps — DAG order via Kahn, not application sort of a flat list
decision branches — YAML eligibility_logic plus remaining Python in rules_engine
implementation_notes.where: ADR already in tree — this JSON cites it. No schema change.

proposals.relopass_payoff: Prevents the lecture-structure-for-everything anti-pattern (trie, BST, linked list) from compounding across corridors. Creates a defensible, documented data architecture.

grounding.do_not: Do not treat WorkspaceDB kg_* names as schema. Verify the live table before writing a load. Do not expand the ADR in this JSON-only pass unless it contradicts the status map.

proposals.title: Demand-Pull Corridor Schema Growth — Enforce No Over-Allocation
proposals.cs_concept: Resizing arrays anti-pattern — never pre-allocate unused slots
proposals.problem_solved: Pre-creating empty requirement rows for unverified corridors wastes schema space and risks an unverified corridor being served if a code path reaches it.
proposals.description: There is no corridor registry table and no anchor_case_id column. Source of truth is corridors/<ID>/corridor.yaml. Demand-pull is enforced as YAML metadata plus the existing review_status='pending' / serve-only-approved gate. New corridor profiles must declare an anchor (real case). Existing 13 profiles are grandfathered.

implementation_notes.implementation: Optional corridor.anchor {case_id | case_ref, note} parsed by corridor_registry. scripts/check_corridor_anchor.py fails PRs that add a new corridors/*/corridor.yaml without it.
implementation_notes.why_it_matters: A NOT NULL on a fictional table would not stop a YAML + approved requirement_items load.
implementation_notes.analogy: The corridor graph grows only when a new verified case is named in git, not when someone pre-allocates empty rows

proposals.relopass_payoff: Enforces no-corridor-without-a-real-case at the YAML layer that actually creates corridors. Serving still fail-closes on unapproved items.

grounding.do_not: Do not ADD COLUMN anchor_case_id NOT NULL on a table that is not the corridor source of truth. Do not pre-create empty requirement_items for unverified corridors.

key_principle: CS50 Lec 5: every data structure trades time against space, and the right choice depends on which operation dominates. ReloPass already has four access patterns — fetch-by-key, ordered traversal, dependency resolution, prefix discovery — each already mapped to a structure. The mistake to avoid is forcing a lecture structure (trie, BST, linked list, fictional hash map) onto those operations, or inventing tables whose names came from the lecture rather than from the live schema.
